Text: Citigroup lines up Wall Street banks for Banamex IPO Citigroup is assembling major Wall Street banks for an IPO of Mexico’s Grupo Financiero Banamex that could raise more than $3 billion, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Citigroup is expected to lead the offering, with Bank of America, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase also involved. The banks are targeting January for the listing. Citigroup and Banamex are still assessing how much of Citi’s remaining stake could be sold before the IPO, with smaller stake sales possible. The plans remain under discussion and could change, while additional banks may join the syndicate. The IPO is part of CEO Jane Fraser’s broader retreat from consumer banking in international markets. Citi sold 25% of Banamex to Mexican billionaire Fernando Chico Pardo last year and another 24% to investors including General Atlantic and Blackstone, leaving it with about 51%. $C $BAC $GS $JPM

Text: U.S. high-yield credit spreads reached their highest level in five months as a surge in corporate debt issuance tests investor demand, according to Goldman Sachs credit strategist Amanda Lynam. September issuance totaled $38.51 billion, making it the busiest month of the year for junk bonds, helped by large deals including SoftBank's $10 billion offering. Lynam said the market is showing signs of the same “indigestion” seen in investment-grade credit earlier this summer. With a heavy issuance calendar and rising bond yields, the extra yield investors demand to hold corporate junk bonds over Treasuries widened 12 basis points to 294 basis points on Friday, the highest since April. Average CCC-rated spreads reached 968 basis points, their highest since November 2023. Goldman has tracked nearly $600 billion of AI-related debt issuance this year, with only about 40% coming from hyperscalers, highlighting the broader exposure across the sector. $GS

Author: topstockalerts
Text: Goldman Sachs’ board has discussed a succession plan under which CEO David Solomon would step down and be replaced by COO and President John Waldron, potentially in late 2027 or 2028, according to The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter. The discussions envision Waldron taking over as CEO while Solomon would likely transition to executive chairman for roughly one to two years after leaving the top executive role. The proposal still requires approval from Goldman’s board and could be finalized in the coming months, although the timing and structure remain subject to change. Solomon has led Goldman for nearly a decade, with his tenure marked by a strong emphasis on the bank’s trading operations and efforts to strengthen its position across financial markets. That strategy has benefited from favorable market conditions in recent years, helping drive strong results and pushing Goldman shares to record highs. $GS
